title: Procedural generation with a seeded random
when: Levels, maps or loot are generated by code and must be reproducible from a seed for daily challenges, bug reports and tests.
prompt:
Goal: All randomness comes from one seeded generator, so the same seed always builds the same world.
Steps:
1. js/rng.mjs: mulberry32(seed) returns a function yielding floats in [0, 1); seedFromString(text) is an FNV 1a hash using Math.imul and >>> 0.
2. Helpers on top: int(min, max) inclusive, pick(array), chance(p) and shuffle(array), all taking the rng.
3. Separate streams: rngMap = mulberry32(seed) and rngLoot = mulberry32(seed ^ 0x9e3779b9), so new loot rules do not change the map.
4. Rooms and corridors: place up to N rooms with limited retries, reject overlaps, join each room to the next with L shaped corridors, then flood fill from the start to confirm every room is reachable.
5. Validate the result (start and exit exist, path length in range); when invalid try seed + 1 and record the attempt count.
6. Show the seed in the pause menu and accept ?seed=word to share runs; the daily seed is the date as YYYY-MM-DD.
Quality bar:
- One seed gives identical level JSON on any machine.
- A 100 by 100 map generates in under 50 ms.
Pitfalls:
- One stray Math.random call that breaks reproducibility.
- Unbounded retry loops when the constraints cannot be met.
- Float hashing that differs across engines; stay in 32 bit integer math.
Verify:
- [ ] node:test: two runs with seed "abc" are deepEqual; "abc" and "abd" differ.
- [ ] 500 random seeds all produce a reachable exit.
Output: js/rng.mjs, js/generate.mjs and test/generate.test.mjs.

examples.input: gerar masmorras aleatórias com semente para desafio diário
examples.output: mulberry32 streams, room and corridor generator with flood fill check, seed sharing, tests
